reason: The midwives Shiphrah and Puah are regular people (workers, not royal or divine figures) who demonstrate clear agency. They make deliberate moral choices—fearing God and refusing to obey Pharaoh's command to kill Hebrew male infants. They take direct action by preserving the babies alive, respond to Pharaoh's interrogation with their own explanation, and their choices have narrative consequences. The text explicitly states 'וַתִּירֶאןָ הַֽמְיַלְּדֹת אֶת־ הָאֱלֹהִים וְלֹא עָשׂוּ' (the midwives feared God and did not do as the king commanded)—affirming their agency in choosing conscience over authority.
